headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 deep into the CME weekend halt as the US-Iran tanker exchange stays unanswered, crude holds a near-10% weekly gain, and a verified Foxconn AI signal leaves the reopening setup two-sided
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having ranged between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions inside that session, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday settle and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on 6 September, which falls after the final slot of this forecast, so the last print remains the only anchor and no published hour can contain observable price action. The Saturday geopolitical sequence is unchanged and still unresolved at this assessment. ABC News reporting confirms that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired ballistic missiles toward a US aircraft carrier and a destroyer, that neither ship was hit and no US personnel were injured, and that US forces permanently disabled two Iranian tankers and destroyed a third under what officials describe as a tanker-for-tanker policy. CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper framed the response as imposing a higher economic cost. No verified Iranian state response to Saturday's strikes and no Strait of Hormuz closure announcement has been reported in the hours since the previous assessment, which is the single most important thing this run can establish: the escalation stack has aged without a new rung. Reuters reports WTI settling at 91.48 dollars and Brent at 96.28 dollars on Friday, with WTI up close to 10% on the week, Brent up 7.6% and US diesel at a record 5.85 dollars per gallon on impaired Middle East supply routes. The macro backdrop stays two-sided. August payrolls rose 162,000 against a consensus near 53,000 with the Dow down 0.51%, the S&P 500 down 0.38% and the Nasdaq Composite down 0.29% on the session even as the Nasdaq-100 closed higher, and published odds of a September rate increase rose with fed funds futures pricing around a 58% chance of a hike. Federal Reserve H.15 data through 3 September shows the 2-year constant maturity at 4.34% and the 10-year at 4.77%, before Friday's payroll-driven move higher. On Friday the President also tied a threatened trade embargo on deficit countries to a demand for Fed rate cuts, an item that remains entirely unpriced. Against that, one genuinely constructive and verified weekend catalyst has arrived: Foxconn, the largest server maker for Nvidia and a major Apple supplier, said on Saturday that third-quarter operations are expected to outperform market expectations as AI demand continues to grow, with August revenue of 921.8 billion Taiwan dollars up about 52% year over year and third-quarter visibility improved on the prior month, while cautioning about volatile global politics. Cross-asset context from the latest completed session is mixed rather than aligned: semiconductor equipment and semiconductors led sharply while application and infrastructure software lagged, communication services and consumer cyclicals were negative, and the VIX closed at 14.53 within a 13.80 to 14.58 range, a low absolute volatility base. Because none of this can express itself while quoting is suspended, the stack is scored as elevated Stress with Tail held at a closed-venue floor. US Labor Day on 7 September means the first cash session after the reopen is 8 September, so the backlog carried into cash price discovery is longer than after a normal weekend. That is published as conditional gap risk for hours beyond this horizon, not as observed structure.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the closing three hours of the August payroll session and the first twenty-one hours of the CME weekend halt. The 18:00 UTC hour on 4 September sat past the release peak at Tail 13% and Stress 51% under a mixed mode, and every slot in this window maps to EA_ON and green. Tail decayed through the remainder of the US cash session as the index gave back its highs and recovered, reaching Tail 12% and Stress 48% by 20:00 UTC with semiconductor leadership diverging from a softer broad tape. From the 21:00 UTC futures settlement onward every hour has been scored at the closed-venue floor of Tail 5% with mode normal, while Stress eased to 38% and then drifted back up through the Saturday hours as the verified US-Iran tanker exchange was reported and the unpriced weekend stack accumulated, reaching 51% by 17:00 UTC. All 24 slots carry a published Claude assessment.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, which does not end until 22:00 UTC on 6 September, roughly five hours after the final published slot, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor, easing to 4% through the dormant middle of the weekend and returning to 5% as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline. Stress opens at 51% and drifts to a 59% peak, inside the elevated band for the whole horizon, reflecting the still-unanswered US-Iran tanker exchange, an energy premium from continued Strait of Hormuz disruption, hawkish September rate pricing after the August payroll beat, an unresolved Friday trade-embargo ultimatum tied to Fed policy, and an open two-sided headline window whose accumulated content would express in a single reopening auction. Mode is characterised as normal through the dormant hours and mixed in the closing hours, where the setup carried toward the reopen is genuinely two-sided: an energy and geopolitical premium and hawkish rate pricing against semiconductor leadership and a verified Saturday AI demand signal from Foxconn. Confidence stays in the high band, easing from 85% to 78% purely as a function of evidence age across a full weekend without a refreshing quote.
